review.tagline: C++ library for similarity search and clustering of dense vectors
review.summary: Faiss is a C++ library with Python/numpy wrappers for nearest-neighbor search over dense vectors using L2 distance, dot product or cosine. It offers exact search, HNSW and NSG graph indexes, and compressed indexes that scale to billions of vectors in memory. Some indexes also run on GPU via CUDA or AMD ROCm, with optional NVIDIA cuVS backends.
review.audience: Engineers embedding vector search in their own C++ or Python applications
strengths: Many index types trading off speed, accuracy, memory per vector and training time
Compressed and binary indexes handle sets that do not fit in RAM uncompressed
GPU indexes (CUDA, ROCm) replace CPU ones, single or multi-GPU
Only hard dependency is a BLAS implementation; MIT licensed
weaknesses: Library only: no server, REST API, auth or built-in persistence service
Vectors are identified by integers; metadata filtering must be built separately
Choosing and tuning an index type requires understanding the trade-offs
Builds with cmake; prebuilt packages are listed for Anaconda only
needs: Needs BLAS, CUDA or ROCm (optional), NVIDIA cuVS (optional)
